preview_en:
A trip to face former club Bournemouth would’ve been a fixture Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola has circled on his calendar, with both sides looking to use the occasion to kickstart their Premier League seasons.

Match News and Current Form

Marco Rose’s tenure at Bournemouth received a much-needed shot in the arm on Thursday as they sealed a historic 2-1 win over Real Sociedad in their first-ever European game. That followed a winless start to the Cherries’ Premier League campaign (D3, L1) in which they surrendered the lead in each fixture, with those results making up part of a tally of 13 draws from their 23 league matches in 2026 (W8, L2) - the highest ratio of stalemates by a team in a single year in the history of the English top flight. They can at least point to being incredibly hard to beat, particularly at home where they’re unbeaten in all competitions since their first fixture of the calendar year (W4, D8).

Liverpool travel to the south coast hoping to keep their unbeaten start to the season (W3, D3) intact after a midweek 3-1 EFL Cup win over Tottenham. Those three draws have all come in the league, most recently being held scoreless by Fulham last week, with the Reds only once before drawing four of their first five league games of a campaign. Clean sheets in their last two league games point to Iraola’s men trending in the right direction, though a return of just two wins from their last nine away matches (D1, L6) must remain an area of concern.

Head-to-Head History

Liverpool have lost just three of the 22 H2Hs this century (W18, D1), but each Bournemouth victory came at the Vitality Stadium, including a 3-2 success in last season's corresponding fixture.

Hot Stats and Streaks

Bournemouth received 2+ yellow cards in eight of their last nine fixtures.

Eleven of Bournemouth’s last 14 home games saw both teams score.

Liverpool have registered at least five shots on target in ten of their last 11 competitive away games.

Eight of Liverpool's last nine domestic away matches featured over 2.5 goals.

Key Players to Watch and Missing Players

Justin Kluivert has hit form with goals in Bournemouth’s last two matches, and has netted his team’s opener in seven of his last nine goalscoring outings. Dominik Szoboszlai ’s confidence will also be sky-high after his outstanding goal in midweek, which was the seventh of his last ten goals for club or country to come after half-time, starting with a goal in this fixture last term.

Neither side seem to have any fresh injury concerns.

For all the latest team news, please check the Flashscore match centre.

Betting Analysis

Nobody knows this Bournemouth side better than Iraola, so backing him to use that experience and guide Liverpool to a win with both teams scoring seems a logical play.

Author: Peter Stavrinou
